summary: Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul J. Griffiths, William K. Mahony, and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young (born 1944) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned an M.A. at the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. at McGill University (~1970–1978), where she later served as Professor (~1978–2015).
Katherine R. Tsiang is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of Chicago, attested in 2012 and as a faculty member in 2026.

Kathleen D. Morrison (born 1963) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, later serving as Assistant Professor at Northwestern University (~1995–1999) and holding a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon (1906–1978) was an archaeologist educated at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College. She held appointments at the University of London (~1935–1962), UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College, Oxford (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at DePauw University, UW-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (~1993–2017).
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 2000 under the doctoral supervision of Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille (born 1948) is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald. She has held posts at EPHE, CRCAO, and as an editor for EMSCAT.

Katragadda Paddayya (born 1943) is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1968) and served as Professor and Professor of Geo-archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1974–2008).

Katrin Querl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. A former student at the University of Vienna, she is attested in 2026 as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin and Tibetan lecturer at the University of Hamburg.

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Tokyo and University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (born 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor at Hanazono University around 1999.

Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita (1874–1946) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held a post there from circa 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki (born 1947) studied Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology at Kyoto University and in Paris. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1992; 1996–2010) and became a member of the Japan Academy in 2006.

Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) studied at the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1988–2009) and directed the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (~1999–2009).

Katsumi Tanabe (born 1941) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1971) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1992–2000) and Chuo University (~2000–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees at Kyoto University, held posts there (1933–1943), at Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and served as professor at Ryukoku University (~1964–1980).

Kausthub Desikachar works in Indology and religious studies. He founded Viniyoga Singapore and KHYF, served as Executive Trustee at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram until 2012, and became Chief Executive, senior teacher, and yoga therapy consultant at KHYF.
